solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Rogue is to pope, as impious is to holy? (8)

annotation.definitionNote: The definition is a relation, not a word: impious is the OPPOSITE of holy.

indicatorNotes.Rogue: rogue as an adjective means wild and out of control, so the letters run riot

annotation.surface: An analogy question from an exam: rogue is to pope as impious is to holy.
annotation.walkthrough: The clue is dressed as a school analogy test, so 'is to' reads as grammar; in fact 'is to pope' is the fodder and only the second half is the definition.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by relation: impious stands at the far end from holy, just as a rogue does from a pope.

entries.clue: St Peter’s successor seemingly concealing maiden[’s] perilous location (7)

indicatorNotes.concealing: to conceal is to hide inside, so the pope's title hides the M within itself

blocks.note: St Peter was the first pope, so his successor would seem to be the second
M = maiden (a maiden over in cricket scoring)

annotation.surface: A tale of the Vatican, with St Peter's heir shielding a young woman from danger.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Seemingly' excuses the joke: St Peter's actual successor was Linus, but POPE II is what the title would look like.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: the Roman town sat beneath Vesuvius and was buried by it in AD 79.

entries.clue: Begrudge supporting old leader of mafia shot here, there and everywhere (11)

indicatorNotes.supporting: in a down clue the word that supports sits underneath, so RESENT comes last
indicatorNotes.leader of: the leader of a word is the letter at its front

blocks.note: a nip is a small shot of spirits

annotation.surface: Someone bitter about an old mob boss who was gunned down.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shot' pulls towards gunfire beside the mafia; it is the drink. RESENT is named first but, 'supporting' the rest in a down entry, it goes at the bottom.
annotation.definitionFit: A paraphrase: the Latin omni- means all, so being present in every place at once.

entries.clue: What’s cast, forgoing other safeguards (5)

indicatorNotes.safeguards: to safeguard is to keep safe inside, so the two words hold the answer

blocks.note: the letters run across the join, from the end of the first word into the start of the second

annotation.surface: A cast of characters, or a spell, dropping its other protections.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Cast' suggests a play or a spell; here it is metal poured into a mould. The answer sits in forgo(ING OT)her.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a bar of metal is made by pouring it molten into a mould.

entries.clue: Harry wanting very spacious case (7)

indicatorNotes.wanting: wanting means lacking, so VEX loses V

blocks.note: to harry is to VEX; without V (very) it leaves EX

annotation.surface: Prince Harry longing for a roomy suitcase.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Harry' looks like the prince, but it is the verb meaning to pester.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym in the sense of 'a case in point', not a container.

entries.clue: Fuss, saying instruction to boxer making comeback? (6)

indicatorNotes.making comeback: to make a comeback is to come back, so the pair is read right to left

blocks.note: a saw is a saying or proverb
a boxer is a breed of dog, told to sit

annotation.surface: A corner man shouting instructions to a boxer staging a comeback fight.
annotation.walkthrough: The boxer is the dog, not the fighter. TISWAS is British slang for a state of agitation, as in 'all of a tiswas'.
annotation.definitionFit: A British colloquial synonym: to be all of a tiswas is to be in a flap.

entries.clue: Restrict man’s starting blocks with pistol [and] stopwatch possibly (9)

indicatorNotes.blocks: to block is to stand in the way, so the M sits inside TIE

blocks.note: piece is slang for a pistol; 'with' just adds it on

annotation.surface: A race starter with his pistol and stopwatch holding the runners in their blocks.
annotation.walkthrough: The athletics scene makes 'starting blocks' one phrase; it splits into 'starting' (first letter) and 'blocks' (goes inside).
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a stopwatch is one kind, hence 'possibly'.

entries.clue: I get tight shorts removed at regular intervals (3)

indicatorNotes.removed at regular intervals: every other letter of shorts is taken away

blocks.note: S h O r T s: the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters stay

annotation.surface: Someone complaining their shorts are too tight and need taking off.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Tight' suggests snug clothing next to shorts; it means drunk, and 'I get tight' is the answer describing itself.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition in the first person: a drunkard speaking, tight being slang for drunk.

entries.clue: Since pinching copy, regret mounts up (7)

indicatorNotes.pinching: AS pinches, or grips, the other letters inside it

blocks.note: cc = copy, as on an email

annotation.surface: A plagiarist whose remorse keeps growing after being caught copying.
annotation.walkthrough: AS holds both CC and RUE, in that order.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, used of interest or debts that build up over time.

entries.clue: Maureen blasted romantic mag showing personal letters (13)

indicatorNotes.blasted: blasted means blown apart, so the letters scatter

annotation.surface: Maureen furiously denouncing a romance magazine for printing private love letters.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Personal letters' suggests private correspondence; they are initials, as embroidered in a monogram.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description: a monogram is a design made of someone's initials.

entries.clue: One who’s fetching display firstly selects the frames (6)

indicatorNotes.firstly: take the first letter of each of the next two words
indicatorNotes.frames: the two letters go round EXPO like a picture frame

blocks.note: first letters of selects and the
an expo is an exhibition or display

annotation.surface: A gallery curator choosing picture frames for an exhibition.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fetching' pulls towards carrying things; it means attractive.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description, using fetching in its sense of alluring.

entries.clue: Dad, mature, with wife leaving Chicago? (3,5)

indicatorNotes.leaving: to leave is to go away, so W walks out of GROWUP

blocks.note: to grow up is to mature
W = wife, taken out of GROWUP

annotation.surface: A father who has grown up and left his wife to move to Chicago.
annotation.walkthrough: Chicago looks like the city; the question mark flags it as an example of a band, the American rock group.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Chicago is an American band, flagged by the question mark.

entries.clue: Protest band from US — one containing guitar (11)

blocks.note: R.E.M. is an American rock band
a Strat is a Fender Stratocaster guitar

annotation.surface: A protest band from America, one of them strumming a guitar.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Protest band' reads as one phrase; the definition is 'Protest' alone, as a verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, with the verb sense of objecting forcefully.

entries.clue: In rhyme, Peter periodically raves about superb peppers (10)

indicatorNotes.periodically: at regular periods, so every other letter of raves
indicatorNotes.about: the letters from raves are set around superb, sitting beside ACE

blocks.note: Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers
r A v E s: the 2nd and 4th letters

annotation.surface: Peter going into occasional raptures about excellent peppers, in a nursery rhyme.
annotation.walkthrough: The rhyme is 'Peter Piper picked a peck of pickled peppers', which also supplies the theme.
annotation.definitionFit: A botanical name: this is the plant family that includes black pepper.

entries.clue: Fabulous man with cape interrupting functions (9)

indicatorNotes.interrupting: to interrupt is to break in, so C breaks into ROLES

annotation.surface: A superhero whose cape keeps getting in the way at parties.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Fabulous' means from a fable, not wonderful: Androcles pulled a thorn from a lion's paw.
annotation.definitionFit: A pun on fabulous: he is the hero of Aesop's fable of the slave and the lion.

entries.clue: For wine, fermentation of this is a sine qua non (4)

blocks.note: freshly pressed grape juice, which ferments into wine
Latin for 'without which not': an essential thing

annotation.surface: A wine buff insisting that fermentation is indispensable.
annotation.walkthrough: The sentence is true twice over: fermenting must is essential for wine, and 'a must' is what sine qua non means.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: the winemaker's term for unfermented grape juice, and the everyday noun for a necessity.

entries.clue: Witch-hunt brushing aside quiet advocate (4)

indicatorNotes.brushing aside: to brush something aside is to dismiss it, so P is swept away

blocks.note: a purge is a witch-hunt against opponents
P = piano, quiet in music; removed

annotation.surface: A witch-hunt that dismisses a softly spoken lawyer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Advocate' looks like a noun, a lawyer; it is the verb.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, taking advocate as a verb: to press for a course of action.

entries.clue: Car missing rear end blocking road over a Welsh river (7)

indicatorNotes.blocking: HOND sits inside RD, blocking the road
indicatorNotes.over: in a down clue the road sits over the A

blocks.note: the car make HONDA without its last letter

annotation.surface: A broken-down car, its back end gone, stuck across a road in Wales.
annotation.walkthrough: The river gives its name to the Rhondda valleys, the old coal-mining country of South Wales.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: a river of Glamorgan in South Wales.

entries.clue: Knock, making audible sound (10)

indicatorNotes.audible: say the two words and you hear the answer

blocks.note: to diss is to knock, or criticise; making money is earning

annotation.surface: A knock at the door that makes a noise you can hear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like a noise beside knock and audible; it is the adjective, as in sound judgement.
annotation.definitionFit: A synonym for sound in its sense of shrewd and well-judged.

entries.clue: Small bank possibly short of pounds? (7)

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing labels
a bank is one kind of lender

annotation.surface: A little bank that has run out of money.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pounds' looks like money beside bank; the definition means pounds of body weight, a slender person being short of them.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic paraphrase: light in body weight, with pounds read as weight rather than money.

entries.clue: Greeting [from] Satan, trifling with me (7)

indicatorNotes.trifling with: to trifle with something is to toy with it, so the letters are played about

annotation.surface: The Devil himself sending a greeting while toying with the speaker.
annotation.walkthrough: Namaste is a Hindu greeting, said with palms pressed together.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: the Hindi salutation used in India and Nepal.

entries.clue: Alphanumeric string of six or seven characters following pseudo key (8)

annotation.definition: Alphanumeric string of six or seven characters

blocks.note: cod as an adjective means sham or mock, as in cod philosophy

annotation.surface: A programmer writing pseudo-code for a string of characters that follows a key.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Pseudo key' reads as a computing term; it splits into COD (fake) and E (a key). British addresses end in one, like SW1A 1AA.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description of the British mail code, the UK equivalent of a US zip code.

entries.clue: Bury doctor going after mentor stripped of title (6)

indicatorNotes.stripped of: MENTOR has MR taken off it
indicatorNotes.going after: to go after is to follow, so MB is placed behind

blocks.note: MB = Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor

annotation.surface: A doctor chasing a mentor who has been stripped of his title, in the town of Bury.
annotation.walkthrough: Bury looks like the Lancashire town at the head of the clue; it is the verb. The title removed is MR, whose letters sit at either end of MENTOR.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: to lay a body in a tomb.

entries.clue: Animated boy discharging bomb finally cuts what wire? (5)

indicatorNotes.discharging: to discharge is to let go, so BART releases a letter
indicatorNotes.finally: finally points at the last letter, the B of bomb
indicatorNotes.cuts: to cut is to slice into, so ART goes inside EH

blocks.note: Bart Simpson without B, the last letter of bomb

annotation.surface: A cartoon boy defusing a bomb and asking which wire to cut.
annotation.walkthrough: The bomb-disposal surface makes 'what wire?' one question, but 'what' is EH. In a British plug the safety wire is called the earth; Americans say ground.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example, flagged by the question mark: one of the three wires in a plug.

entries.clue: Work [is] due, dream life’s ruined (3,10)

indicatorNotes.ruined: the letters are wrecked and rebuilt

annotation.surface: Someone with work due, whose dream life is wrecked by the deadline.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Work' sounds like a job; it is an artistic work, Johann Strauss's operetta.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by category: an operetta by Johann Strauss II is a musical work.

entries.clue: Say, goose’s beginning (3)

indicatorNotes.’s beginning: the beginning of goose is its first letter

annotation.surface: A riddle about which came first.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Goose's beginning' does both jobs on purpose: its first letter is G, and every goose starts out in a shell.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: the start of a goose's life, read literally.

entries.clue: Almost entirely like Wyrd Sister[’s] mix of meaty morsels (6)

indicatorNotes.Almost entirely: almost all the word, so its last letter is dropped

blocks.note: the Wyrd Sisters are the witches in Macbeth; like a hag = haggish

annotation.surface: A Macbeth witch stirring a cauldron of meaty scraps.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wyrd Sister' is Shakespeare's and Terry Pratchett's name for a witch, or hag.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by description of the Scottish dish of minced sheep's offal, oatmeal and suet.

entries.clue: Hard drug injected in wound made good, at last? (8)

indicatorNotes.injected in: the drug letters are injected into REELED

blocks.note: wound (rhymes with sound), as a fishing line is reeled in

annotation.surface: A hard drug injected into a wound that has finally healed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Wound' looks like an injury beside 'injected', but it is the past tense of wind. A last is a cobbler's foot-shaped mould.
annotation.definitionFit: A cryptic description: a shoe mended on the cobbler's last with new heels.
